concern: vep_seed.csv strand column and the CYP2C19*4 consequence/HGVS annotation
stakes: FIXTURE PROVENANCE, not a shipped user-facing error. Production builds the VEP table from the real bundle; this CSV seeds mini_vep_bundle.db, a TEST ORACLE whose rows are copied into annotated_variants unchanged in tests. The defect is that the oracle disagreed with the reference assembly, so tests could not detect a real regression in the same fields. The 2026-09-05 review found the same row's coordinate also disagreed with GRCh37 (C3).

C1.statement: 19 of the 57 annotated genes carried the wrong genomic strand.
C1.independence: Two annotation projects run by different organisations (EMBL-EBI/Ensembl and NCBI/RefSeq) over the same reference assembly, with separate gene-model pipelines. They are not fully independent -- both are anchored to the same assembly -- but neither imports the other's strand call, unlike the Ensembl-imports-dbSNP case. All 57 resolved through Ensembl with zero fetch failures; all 19 corrected genes re-checked through NCBI Gene with ZERO disagreements.
C1.self_proving_subset: 4 of the 19 (CYP2C19, MTHFR, PON1, CYP2R1) carried BOTH strands on different rows of the same gene. That is impossible for a real gene and needs no external source at all.

C2.statement: rs28399504 (CYP2C19*4, c.1A>G) is start_lost / p.Met1?, not missense_variant / p.Met1Val.
sources: Ensembl GRCh37 VEP on ENST00000371321 (the transcript the row itself cites)
C2.evidence: consequence_terms ['start_lost'], impact HIGH, strand 1; with hgvs=1: hgvsc ENST00000371321.3:c.1A>G, hgvsp ENSP00000360372.3:p.Met1?. The HGVS strings were read from the payload, not copied from the issue. The same payload reports seq_region_name 10, start 96522463, assembly_name GRCh37.
C2.single_source_note: One source, and deliberately so: this is not a contested biological claim but the output of the annotation tool the fixture is supposed to mirror. VEP's call on the cited transcript IS the oracle. A second opinion would be answering a different question.

C3.statement: rs28399504 sits at GRCh37 10:96522463; the fixture row carried 10:94781859.
sources: Ensembl GRCh37 VEP on rs28399504 (seq_region_name / start / assembly_name in both retained payloads)
C3.evidence: Both retained VEP payloads report seq_region_name 10, start 96522463, end 96522463, assembly_name GRCh37. 94781859 falls inside the CYP2C19 span the retained NCBI esummary reports on NC_000010.11 (genomicinfo chrstart 94762680 - chrstop 94855546), i.e. a different assembly release, and mini_vep_bundle.db repeated it. The annotation engine derives ref/alt and zygosity only from a VEP row at the sample's own coordinate, so a GRCh37 sample would match the rsID and lose carriage.
C3.added: 2026-09-05 after review of #2364. Corrected in vep_seed.csv and the regenerated mini_vep_bundle.db; the production-path test seeds the sample at 96522463. No other row's coordinate was audited by this packet; filed separately.

file_shape.actual: 679 rows (678 unique rsIDs: rs121913529 appears twice, alt G>A and G>C, both PAH), of which 100 carry a gene_symbol (99 unique rsIDs)

explicitly_not_claimed: The retained consequence audit was requested once per unique rsID (678). It holds 677 reduced responses and one recorded failure, rs5778923 (HTTP 400; an unannotated intron_variant row on chrX with no gene_symbol), which a 2026-09-05 retry reproduced with the body "No variant found with ID 'rs5778923'" (retained verbatim) -- so the audit does NOT cover that row and it is an exclusion, not a response. Of the 100 annotated rows (99 unique rsIDs; rs5778923 is not among them): 52 agree, 15 disagree on the fixture's own transcript, and 33 rows (32 rsIDs; rs121913529 on both of its rows) cite a transcript Ensembl VEP does not report for that variant. ONLY rs28399504 is corrected here. The other 14 mismatches are predominantly 5_prime_UTR_variant vs upstream_gene_variant, which turn on transcript selection rather than being outright errors, and the 33 unresolvable transcripts need per-row adjudication (transcript version, assembly, MANE choice). Adjudicating 47 rows off one REST call each would be exactly the kind of bulk edit this issue is about. Filed separately.

payload_integrity: Eight payloads are unedited verbatim API responses: the 678 Ensembl GRCh37 VEP responses (677 HTTP 200, one HTTP 400) retained as gzip-compressed JSON Lines with the per-line {rsid, status, response} wrapper as the only addition; two Ensembl VEP records and one NCBI PubMed eSummary captured on the dates their rows give; three captured 2026-09-05 (Ensembl lookup/symbol for the 57 genes; NCBI Gene esearch and esummary for the 19 corrected genes), each a per-symbol map of response objects whose `_artifact_note` and `responses` wrapper are the only additions; and the 48-byte HTTP 400 error body Ensembl GRCh37 VEP returned for rs5778923 on 2026-09-05, stored exactly as received. One payload, the NCBI PubMed EFetch XML for the two cited papers, is SANITIZED: <Abstract> elements were removed under the bibliographic-metadata-only retention rule, and the two author email addresses that its <Affiliation> text carried were replaced by the token [email redacted] with the surrounding affiliation text intact; nothing else was touched, and it is labelled as such in its filename. No other retained payload contains an email address (regex-checked across raw/, the README and this manifest). Five payloads are DERIVED records, labelled as such in the manifest: the lookup/symbol reduction selects each gene's strand and id from the verbatim response; the NCBI Gene reduction selects the live record's uid and genomicinfo coordinates and COMPUTES an orientation from their order; the consequence audit reduces the 677 retained VEP responses (one per unique rsID; 678 requested, the failed rs5778923 recorded under `failures`) to the fixture consequence, the transcript-matched terms and most_severe_consequence, and was re-derived from the retained file on 2026-09-06; the PubMed reduction lists each cited record's CommentsCorrections and publication types; and the Scite record holds the two cited DOIs' metadata and notice status (no HTTP response to capture). Each derived row names the verbatim payload it derives from and the fields it selects. No payload required further sanitization: all are public reference-annotation or bibliographic records with no genotype, sample or personal data.
